title: Know Your Rights: WRCLS Tenancy Legal Session #2
description: Finding a place to live as a student can be overwhelming, from rising rent costs and unclear lease terms to questions about maintenance, deposits, and additional fees. Understanding your rights as a tenant is essential to protecting yourself and avoiding unnecessary stress. But you don’t have to figure it out alone. WUSA is here to help. We’ve teamed up with Waterloo Region Community Legal Services (WRCLS) to offer free virtual (Zoom) legal support clinics to help you get the clarity you need. What to Expect: 50-minute presentation covering key tenancy laws and common issues students face 10-minute Q&A session to ask general legal questions Five private 30-minute one-on-one consultations with a qualified WRCLS lawyer following the presentation (limited availability) To sign up for a one-on-one consultation, email David at drkuhn@wusa.ca with the subject line “WCRLS Legal Session: Consultation Booking” with your name and request to book a consultation. Spots for the one-on-one consultations are limited! To attend the presentation on the 30th, click the Zoom Link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82810623651 👉To sign up for the presentation and Q&A session, RSVP to save your spot. If you’ve got any questions or need some guidance, this is a great chance to get answers. We’re here to help you understand your rights and avoid any unnecessary surprises when it comes to renting.

description: Think you’ve got what it takes to be crowned trivia champ? 👑 Grab your friends—or join a table when you arrive—and get ready for a night full of laughs, friendly competition, and your shot at $150 in Uptown Dollars gift cards for the winning team of each of the 3 rounds!🏆 📍 Where: The Bomber 🗓️ When: Tuesday, March 31 | 7–9 PM Trivia topics include: 🎬 Pop Culture & Film🎵 Music📺 TV🍿 Snacks & More! title: Politics Without the Podium 2026
tags: @yourwusa, Advocacy, Events, student advocacy, students, undergrad, WUSA
description: Ever wish you could talk to local leaders without the formal speeches or staged events? Politics Without the Podium creates a relaxed space for students to connect directly with the people shaping the Waterloo community. Join fellow students for an informal evening with Dorothy McCabe, Mayor of Waterloo, and Colleen James, Regional Councillor for the Region of Waterloo. Ask questions, share your perspective, and hear about the issues affecting the region, from housing and transit to community priorities. This event begins with a short introduction and moderated Q&A, followed by open mingling where students can chat directly with the Mayor and Councillor in a casual setting. Come by, grab some free bar food while it lasts, and take part in real conversations about the community where you live and study.
